issues.title: Repo-wide gate scan re-enables the per-hand-off spam whenever ANY other work item is parked at a gate
issues.description: gogo_notify_gates() (hooks/notify.sh:125-145) scans EVERY .gogo/work/*/state.md, so the gate-conditional branch fires for an open gate that has nothing to do with the running pipeline. Verified live in this repo, not hypothetically: `feature-interactive-plan-review` currently reads `awaiting-plan-acceptance` with a written plan.md (8 `## ` sections), and `printf '{"notification_type":"agent_completed","message":"gogo-reviewer finished"}' | GOGO_NOTIFY_DEBUG=1 CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$PWD bash hooks/notify.sh` prints `class=gate verdict=notify gates=1 channels=banner`. So a full /gogo:go on THIS feature today emits one ping per subagent hand-off (3-6 per run), every one reading `feature-interactive-plan-review · awaiting-plan-acceptance` - i.e. the exact reported symptom the feature exists to remove, and a direct falsification of plan.md's acceptance signal ("a full /gogo:go run from plan-accepted to awaiting-uat produces exactly one notification"). A repo with a parked gate is the NORMAL state of an active gogo tree, so the regression is the common case, not the corner. The plan foresaw this precisely: alternative A4 (rate-limit/dedupe) was parked with "keep it in the back pocket only if spam survives the classifier". It survived.
issues.proposed_solution: NEEDS-USER-DECISION - the remedy is a rule choice, not a bug fix, and each option changes what a ping means: (a) SCOPE - count only the gate whose feature folder matches the running session's slug (derivable from the tmux session name `gogo-go-<slug>` or a GOGO_SLUG the orchestrator exports), so an unrelated parked item never pings; (b) EDGE - ping only when the gate set CHANGED since the previous invocation, which needs the mutable state under .gogo/ the plan put out of scope; (c) A4 - dedupe/rate-limit identical gate messages within a window; (d) ACCEPT the behaviour and correct plan.md's acceptance signal to "exactly one notification per newly-opened gate, given no other item is parked". Recommendation: (a) - it is the only option that keeps the acceptance signal literally true, adds no mutable state, and still pings for the item you are actually running. Whichever is chosen, re-run the dogfood E2E in a tree that HAS a parked gate; the current one does, so the evidence is already reproducible.
issues.fix_summary: D4 resolved by the user: edge-latch. The gate-conditional branch now pings only for gates NOT in the last-notified set (.gogo/.notify-gates, rewritten pruned each gate-class invocation; missing/unreadable file degrades to fire-on-open-gate). Verified live: parked-gate repo pings once then stays silent; closed gate prunes. 4 new selftest cases (41/41 both bashes). --- VERIFIED (round 2, fresh reviewer): reproduced independently in a temp tree with one parked awaiting-plan-acceptance gate - 4 consecutive agent_completed hand-offs give notify,silent,silent,silent (HEAD) where the pre-D4 shape gives notify,notify,notify,notify. Also verified: closing the gate prunes the seen file to empty and re-opening it re-pings; an empty / truncated / unreadable seen file degrades to notify (never to silence); 8 concurrent invocations against a cold latch produce exactly 1 notify + 7 silent (a race can only duplicate a ping, never drop one); grep -Fxv -f handles the UTF-8 middot identically under LC_ALL=C, POSIX and en_US.UTF-8 on BSD grep. See REV-010: the latch's WRITE half has no test that bites.

issues.title: osascript escaping is quote-only, so a backslash in the message injects AppleScript and executes arbitrary shell
issues.description: hooks/notify.sh:209 builds the AppleScript source by string interpolation with `${msg//\"/\\\"}` - it escapes double quotes but NOT backslashes. A message containing `\"` therefore renders as `\\\"`, which AppleScript reads as an escaped backslash FOLLOWED BY THE CLOSING DELIMITER: the string literal ends early and everything after it is parsed as AppleScript code, with a trailing `--` commenting out the harness's own ` with title "..."` tail. VERIFIED with a harmless probe using the exact same escaping expression: a message of `x\" & (do shell script (ASCII character 105 & ASCII character 100)) --` ran `id` and exited 0, while the same shape with chars 122,122,122 exited 1 with `execution error: sh: zzz: command not found (127)` - proving the shell command genuinely executed, not merely compiled. `ASCII character` is used only to avoid needing a quote character in the payload; no quote is required to reach `do shell script`. The same hole exists on `$title` via the cwd basename. This shape is pre-existing (identical line at HEAD), but the file is being rewritten wholesale here and the plan deliberately widens what reaches `msg` ("the body is either Claude's own message ... or a named gate"), so it is in scope for this review. coding-rules.md's injection-safety bar and the review standards' security dimension both bite.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Escape the backslash FIRST, then the quote, for both fields: `local m="${msg//\\/\\\\}"; m="${m//\"/\\\"}"` and the same for the title, then interpolate `$m`. Or, better, stop interpolating into the script text at all - pass the strings as argv: `osascript - "$msg" "$title" >/dev/null 2>&1 <<'AS' || true` / `on run argv` / `display notification (item 1 of argv) with title (item 2 of argv)` / `end run` / `AS`. The argv form has no escaping surface at all. Add a selftest case pinning that a message containing a backslash-quote is neutralised (assert the escaped string, since the send path itself must stay side-effect-free).
issues.fix_summary: osascript now receives msg/title as argv via an on-run-argv heredoc - no interpolation into AppleScript source, no escaping surface; covered end-to-end by the DRYRUN selftest cases --- VERIFIED (round 2): notify.sh:246-250 uses a quoted heredoc ('AS') with `osascript - "$msg" "$title"` and `item 1 of argv`, so no payload byte reaches the AppleScript source. Re-ran round 1's exploit against HEAD in both shapes - a quote-terminated `& (do shell script "touch /tmp/GOGO_PWNED") & "` payload and a backslash-quote `y\\" & ... --` payload - each exits 0 with channels=banner and NEITHER probe file is created. The injection is structurally gone, not merely escaped.

issues.title: The FR8 anti-drift guard is blind in its primary direction: a new gate status in contract.WaitingForInput() keeps it green
issues.description: cli/notify_hook_test.go:41-95 derives the expected gate set by running the status enum through contract.WaitingForInput() - but it reads that ENUM from templates/state.template.md's legend comment, not from the contract. So the only drift it detects is one that also lands in the template. VERIFIED by mutation: adding `"awaiting-security-signoff"` to the `case "waiting-for-user", "awaiting-uat":` arm of contract.go:174 (leaving hooks/notify.sh and the template untouched) leaves `go test -run TestNotifyHookGateStatusesMatchContract` reporting `ok` - the exact drift the guard exists to catch. `want` silently shrinks to whatever the template happens to list, so the comparison is with a hand-maintained list, not with the predicate. That undercuts the plan's stated reason for choosing this approach ("FR8's guard makes the bash copy provably identical rather than merely intended to be (TEST-006's lesson, applied)") and the test's own docstring ("derived by running every status ... never hand-copied"). No other test in cli/ pins the template legend against the code, so the hole is unmitigated (grep: cli_enum_test.go covers commands only).
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add a third source so `want` cannot shrink silently: source-scan cli/internal/contract/contract.go for the quoted status literals inside the WaitingForInput function body (slice between `func (f *Feature) WaitingForInput()` and the closing brace, regexp `"([a-z][a-z-]+)"`), and t.Fatalf if any of them is absent from the enum parsed out of the template - with the usual vacuity guard (fail if the scan finds zero literals, per the `TestNewFormIsTheOnlyFormConstructionSite` precedent in coding-rules.md). Re-run the mutation above to prove the fixed guard now fails.
issues.fix_summary: guard gained a third source: source-scans WaitingForInput() body literals and requires each in the template enum (vacuity-guarded); mutation re-run now FAILs with the drift named --- VERIFIED (round 2): cli/notify_hook_test.go:79-106 adds step 2b with the vacuity guard at :99. Re-ran round 1's exact mutation (added "awaiting-security-signoff" to the case arm in contract.go, template + notify.sh untouched): the guard now FAILs with `contract.WaitingForInput() names "awaiting-security-signoff", which is missing from templates/state.template.md's status enum`. contract.go restored; suite green after. The subtractive direction stays covered by the step-4 set equality, so both drift directions now bite.

issues.title: Both FR5 parse-trap selftest cases pass for a weaker reason than claimed - deleting either mechanism keeps the selftest 33/33
issues.description:
code-review-standards.md #11(c) verbatim: "the test passed for a weaker reason than it claimed". Both FR5 traps the plan's Tests table names as covered are vacuous. VERIFIED by mutation on a copy of the script (production code is CORRECT in both cases; only the fixtures are weak):
(1) FIRST-TOKEN SPLIT. Replacing `split(line, a, /[[:space:]]+/); print a[1]` with `print line` (notify.sh:103-104) still yields `selftest: 33/33 passed`, exit 0. The `- **status:** implementing   <!-- awaiting-plan-acceptance | ... -->` fixture (notify.sh:268-269) is defeated by the earlier inline-comment SPLICE, not by the split; no fixture has a status value carrying a trailing token. The split does matter - contract.firstToken exists because "enum-like keys must not carry a trailing (...) note" - and a probe confirms `- **status:** awaiting-uat (uat round 2)` correctly yields a gate today. Nothing pins it.
(2) MULTI-LINE COMMENT BLOCK. Deleting the whole `incomment { if (index(line, "-->")) { incomment = 0 } next }` rule (notify.sh:91-94) also still yields `33/33`. The feature-b fixture's commented example line is INDENTED (`'  - **status:** awaiting-uat'`, notify.sh:274) and the awk pattern `^- \*\*status:\*\*` is column-anchored, so the anchor rejects it whether or not comment tracking exists. The real TEST-001 shape - which the Go parser's docstring reproduces - is un-indented at column 0.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, fixtures only. (1) Add a gate-root fixture with a trailing note, e.g. mk_state "$tmp/gate-note" feature-n '- **status:** awaiting-uat (uat round 2)' and `expect completed-note "$tmp/gate-note" gates "$p_completed" notify 'feature-n · awaiting-uat'` - it fails the moment the split is removed. (2) Change feature-b's commented example line from '  - **status:** awaiting-uat' to column-0 '- **status:** awaiting-uat' so the comment tracking is the only thing that can suppress it. Re-run both mutations after the change and confirm each now drops the selftest below 33 and exits 1.
issues.fix_summary: gate-note fixture pins the first-token split, feature-b commented example moved to column 0 so only comment tracking suppresses it; both mutations re-run: 36/37 and 31/37, exit 1 --- VERIFIED (round 2) by re-running both mutations against the CURRENT 41-case script: (1) replacing the split with `print line` -> `FAIL completed-note: verdict=silent want=notify`, 40/41, exit 1; (2) deleting the `incomment {...}` awk rule -> 35/41, exit 1, with feature-b's commented example leaking as `feature-b · awaiting-uat` into empty-payload, garbage-payload and e2e-silent. Both mechanisms are now load-bearing AND pinned.

issues.title: gogo_state_status is stricter than the parser it mirrors - an indented or loosely-spaced status line becomes a SILENT gate
issues.description: FR5 says the scan mirrors contract.WaitingForInput() exactly, and the state.md grammar is owned by contract.stateLine (cli/internal/contract/state.go:15): `^\s*-\s*\*\*([^:*]+):\*\*\s*(.*)$` - it tolerates leading whitespace and any spacing after the dash. The awk in notify.sh:101-102 requires the literal `^- **status:**`. VERIFIED: for `  - **status:** awaiting-uat` and for `-  **status:** awaiting-uat`, gogo_state_status prints EMPTY, so gogo_notify_gates skips the folder entirely - while the CLI reads both as a genuine open gate (board, `gogo status` WAIT column, the ⏸ pill). The result is a gate the user is never pinged about, which is exactly the failure mode D1 chose gate-conditional unknown types to avoid, on a file that is written by an LLM following prose. It is a degradation to MISSING rather than WRONG, but for a notifier missing means silence, and the divergence is from the single authority FR5 names.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, two lines. Relax the awk to mirror stateLine: `if (line ~ /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*\*\*status:\*\*/)` and `sub(/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*\*\*status:\*\*[[:space:]]*/, "", line)`. Note this makes REV-004(2)'s indented fixture a genuine gate line, so land REV-004's column-0 fixture change together with this one - after both, the comment-block tracking is load-bearing AND pinned.
issues.fix_summary: awk match+sub relaxed to mirror contract.stateLine (leading/loose whitespace tolerated); pinned by the new gate-indent fixture --- VERIFIED (round 2): notify.sh:104-105 now uses the `^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*\*\*status:\*\*` match and the matching sub. Probed all three shapes end to end through the whole script: `  - **status:** awaiting-uat`, `-  **status:** awaiting-uat` and `   -   **status:**   waiting-for-user  ` (trailing spaces) each yield verdict=notify. The gate-indent fixture pins the first shape.

issues.title: curl -d "$msg" treats a message that starts with @ as a filename, pushing file contents to the ntfy topic
issues.description: hooks/notify.sh:202 passes the notification body as `-d "$msg"`. curl documents a leading `@` as "the rest should be a file name to read the data from". VERIFIED against a local listener: `curl -d "@/tmp/gogo-curl-probe.txt" http://127.0.0.1:8931/topic` produced `Content-Length: 20` with body `SECRET-FILE-CONTENTS` - the file, not the literal string. So a notification message beginning with `@` sends the wrong body, and if the text after `@` names an existing readable path it POSTs that file's contents to the ntfy.sh topic (a URL that leaves the machine). Pre-existing shape, low likelihood with today's message sources, but the fix is one flag and this hook now routes payload text and folder names into that body by design.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Use `--data-raw "$msg"` (curl >= 7.43; macOS ships 8.7.1 - verified), which never interprets `@`. If an older curl must be tolerated, `--data-binary @- <<<"$msg"` is the portable equivalent. Keep the trailing `|| true`; a curl too old for the flag then degrades to no push, which the portability bar already allows.
issues.fix_summary: curl -d replaced with --data-raw so a leading @ is never a filename --- VERIFIED (round 2): notify.sh:235 reads `--data-raw "$msg"` with the rationale in the comment above it. Re-ran round 1's local-listener probe with the new flag: the request body is the literal string `@/tmp/gogo-curl-probe.txt` and grep for the file's contents in the captured request returns 0 hits. Exfiltration path closed.

issues.title: Nothing tests the hook end to end - --selftest stops at gogo_notify_decide, so the main glue and the verdict->send dispatch ship unpinned
issues.description: code-review-standards.md #11(b): "a wiring was named in the plan, shipped, and had no test that bites". `--selftest` calls gogo_notify_decide directly (notify.sh:297) - correct, it is the production function, not a copy - but nothing exercises gogo_notify_main (notify.sh:221-241): the `payload="$(cat)"` read, the subtle `IFS=$'\t' read -r class verdict gates msg <<EOF $(gogo_notify_decide "$payload") EOF` record parse, the `[ "$verdict" = "notify" ]` dispatch, the channel roll-up, or the exit-0 guarantee. If that record parse broke, `verdict` would read empty, the hook would go permanently silent, and both Go tests plus the 33-case selftest would stay green. I confirmed the glue works today by piping a payload through the script by hand (`class=gate verdict=notify gates=1 channels=banner`, exit 0) - that manual check is the only coverage it has.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add a dry-run seam: `GOGO_NOTIFY_DRYRUN=1` makes gogo_notify_send print the channels it WOULD use and return, without invoking curl/osascript//dev/tty (one guard clause at the top of the function). Then add two selftest cases that run the script itself - `printf '%s' "$p_completed" | GOGO_NOTIFY_DRYRUN=1 GOGO_NOTIFY_DEBUG=1 CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$tmp/gate-uat" bash "$0" 2>&1` - asserting the trace line contains `verdict=notify` and a non-`none` channel list, and the mirror case against "$tmp/quiet" asserting `verdict=silent`; assert exit 0 in both. That pins stdin handling, the record parse, the dispatch and the exit contract in one shot, still sending nothing.
issues.fix_summary: GOGO_NOTIFY_DRYRUN=1 seam in gogo_notify_send + two whole-script selftest cases (stdin -> record parse -> dispatch -> exit 0) asserting the verdict trace both ways --- VERIFIED (round 2): notify.sh:462-484 runs the real script over stdin in both directions. Confirmed the glue is genuinely pinned by mutation: forcing gogo_notify_main to `exit 7` produces `FAIL e2e-notify: exit=7` + `FAIL e2e-silent: exit=7`, 39/41, exit 1 - so the exit-0 contract bites (set -e is suspended inside gogo_selftest because it runs as an `if` condition, which is what keeps the rc assertions reachable). Nothing is sent: DRYRUN reports channels without invoking curl/osascript/tty. NOTE: the seam's write-skip is what leaves the latch write unpinned - raised separately as REV-010, not a regression of this fix.

issues.title: skills/gogo/SKILL.md still carries the un-updated twin of the sentence this change rewrote in docs/flow.md
issues.description: docs/flow.md:208 was updated from "The Notification hook pings the user." to name which events ping. skills/gogo/SKILL.md:405 carries the identical sentence at the identical decision-gate step and was not touched. The statement stays TRUE there (a decision gate writes waiting-for-user, so the gate scan fires), which is why this is not a stale-behaviour major - but code-review-standards.md #1 requires every surface that describes the changed behaviour to be in sync, and the plan's own enumeration-sync grep (plan.md:318-320) listed README.md, docs/, hooks/ and .gogo/knowledge/ while omitting skills/ - which is why it was missed. Full re-grep of `notify.sh|GOGO_NTFY|GOGO_NOTIFY|Notification hook` across README/docs/skills/knowledge/agents/hooks/templates found exactly this one un-covered hit; docs/architecture.md:137, .gogo/knowledge/project-knowledge.md:43 and testing-tools.md:25 are all correctly deferred to the phase-5 reconcile by plan.md:314-316.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Mirror the flow.md clause at skills/gogo/SKILL.md:405, e.g. "The Notification hook pings the user (a decision gate writes `waiting-for-user`, so the gate scan fires; see docs/flow.md)." Add `skills/` to the plan's enumeration-sync grep list so the next hook change sweeps it.
issues.fix_summary: skills/gogo/SKILL.md:405 now mirrors the docs/flow.md clause; plan enumeration-sync grep list gained skills/ --- VERIFIED (round 2): SKILL.md:405-406 reads "The Notification hook pings the user (a decision gate writes `waiting-for-user`, so its gate scan fires; see docs/flow.md)" and plan.md:325-327 records the as-built correction adding skills/ to the sweep. Re-ran the full sweep myself over README.md docs/ hooks/ skills/ .gogo/knowledge/ agents/ templates/: the only remaining hits are the three phase-5-deferred ones the plan already lists (docs/architecture.md:137, project-knowledge.md, testing-tools.md:25). The abbreviated SKILL.md clause omits the latch, but a transition INTO waiting-for-user is by construction a newly-opened gate and the sentence cross-links to flow.md, which carries the full latch clause - true as written.

issues.title: The gate scan globs every .gogo/work/*/ dir, but contract.LoadRepo only counts feature-* dirs
issues.description: gogo_notify_gates (notify.sh:128) iterates `"$root"/.gogo/work/*/` while contract.LoadRepo (contract.go:261-263) skips any entry without the `feature-` prefix. VERIFIED: a `.gogo/work/scratchpad/state.md` reading `- **status:** awaiting-uat` yields `scratchpad · awaiting-uat` from gogo_notify_gates, a gate no CLI reader will ever show. Harmless today (nothing in gogo creates a non-feature dir there), but it is a mirror divergence in the same FR5 predicate REV-003/REV-005 cover, and the fix is one glob.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, one line: `for dir in "$root"/.gogo/work/feature-*/`. The existing `[ -d "$dir" ] || continue` already absorbs the no-match literal, so the no-.gogo degradation path is unchanged.
issues.fix_summary: gate scan glob narrowed to .gogo/work/feature-*/ matching contract.LoadRepo --- VERIFIED (round 2): notify.sh:131 globs `"$root"/.gogo/work/feature-*/`. Re-ran round 1's probe - a `.gogo/work/scratchpad/state.md` reading `- **status:** awaiting-uat` now yields `verdict=silent gates=0`. The `[ -d "$dir" ] || continue` guard still absorbs the no-match literal (the empty-root selftest case stays green).

issues.title: The D4 latch's WRITE half is unpinned: deleting gogo_notify_remember() from main keeps the selftest 41/41 green while silently restoring REV-001's per-hand-off spam
issues.description: code-review-standards.md #11(b) verbatim - "a wiring was named in the plan, shipped, and had no test that bites" - and it is the wiring that carries the whole D4 fix. PROVEN BY MUTATION: deleting the three-line block at hooks/notify.sh:294-296 (`if [ "${GOGO_NOTIFY_DRYRUN:-}" != "1" ]; then gogo_notify_remember "$root" "$current"; fi`) leaves `bash hooks/notify.sh --selftest` at **41/41 passed, exit 0**, gofmt/vet/`go test ./...` all green - while the mutant reproduces REV-001 exactly: against a temp tree with one parked `awaiting-plan-acceptance` gate, four consecutive `agent_completed` hand-offs give notify,notify,notify,notify (HEAD gives notify,silent,silent,silent). Without the write the seen file is never created, so `gogo_notify_new_gates`'s `[ ! -s "$seen" ]` branch reports every open gate as new, forever. ROOT CAUSE: the DRYRUN seam added for REV-007 is the very flag that disables the write, and **all four** whole-script selftest invocations (notify.sh:466, 476, 491, 501) set `GOGO_NOTIFY_DRYRUN=1` - so the production write path is structurally unreachable from the test suite. The `latch-remember` case at notify.sh:509-515 calls `gogo_notify_remember` directly as a unit and therefore cannot see the missing call site; the `latch-seen` case passes only because the test hand-writes `.notify-gates` itself at notify.sh:499. Cross-check: mutating `gogo_notify_new_gates` to always return everything DOES bite (39/41), so the read half is pinned and only the write half is not.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Make DRYRUN mean "send nothing", not "remember nothing" - the write already targets a per-case temp `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, so it is repeatable. Drop the DRYRUN guard around `gogo_notify_remember` at notify.sh:294-296 (leave the guard inside `gogo_notify_send`, which is the real side effect), then add ONE end-to-end case in a fresh latch root that runs the script TWICE with no hand-written seen file and asserts notify then silent, plus an assertion that `$latch_root/.gogo/.notify-gates` holds the current gate set after the first run. Adjust `latch-first`/`latch-seen` to stop pre-writing the file. Re-run the mutation above and confirm the suite now drops below 41 and exits 1 - that is the acceptance criterion for this fix. (Do NOT settle for a comment; the standard requires the assertion to bite.)
issues.fix_summary: DRYRUN now means send-nothing only: the remember write runs unconditionally in main (fed by decide 5th-field gatelist, no re-scan). Latch e2e restructured with NO hand-written state: run1 notify + latch-wrote asserts the SCRIPT wrote the seen file, run2 silent. Acceptance mutation re-run (remember call no-op) -> 39/42, exit 1: the write half now bites. --- VERIFIED (round 3, fresh reviewer): the acceptance criterion this finding set for itself is met. notify.sh:296-299 calls gogo_notify_remember UNCONDITIONALLY for class=gate at level=gates (the DRYRUN guard is gone; it survives only inside gogo_notify_send), fed by decide's new 5th record field so no second scan is needed, and the knob header (notify.sh:27-28) states the trade-off truthfully: "never SEND (probes/selftest). The latch file is still updated - a dry run is still an invocation." Re-ran the prescribed mutation independently: no-op'ing the remember call site -> 39/42, exit 1, with latch-wrote, latch-seen and latch-diff all failing. The complementary mutation (forcing gogo_notify_new_gates down its degrade branch) -> 40/42, so BOTH halves of the latch are now pinned. The rebuilt e2e cases hand-write no state: latch-wrote (notify.sh:502-506) asserts the SCRIPT itself created .gogo/resources/notify/gates holding exactly the set it pinged about. Live lifecycle re-checked in a temp tree (2 gates): open -> notify(2), repeat -> silent, close one -> seen pruned to the survivor, close both -> file truncated to 0 bytes, reopen -> notify again.

issues.title: A read-only .gogo/ makes the hook print a raw bash redirection error to stderr on every gate-class notification - the misplaced 2>/dev/null never fires
issues.description: `gogo_notify_remember` (hooks/notify.sh:169 and :171) writes `printf '%s\n' "$current" > "$root/.gogo/.notify-gates" 2>/dev/null || true`. Bash applies redirections left to right, so when `>` fails the diagnostic is emitted BEFORE `2>/dev/null` is installed and goes to the real stderr. VERIFIED: with `chmod 555 .gogo` and one open gate, `printf '{"notification_type":"agent_completed"}' | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$T bash hooks/notify.sh` exits 0 but writes `hooks/notify.sh: line 169: /.../.gogo/.notify-gates: Permission denied` to stderr - on EVERY such event, unconditionally, with no GOGO_NOTIFY_DEBUG set. That contradicts three standing bars at once: coding-rules.md Style ("Bash hooks: ... silent no-op when a tool is absent"), non-functional-requirements.md Safety ("Hooks are best-effort and side-effect-light"), and FR6, which promises the hook writes exactly one stderr line per invocation ONLY under `GOGO_NOTIFY_DEBUG=1`. It also contradicts the function's own comment ("Best-effort - an unwritable .gogo/ must never fail the hook"): it does not fail, but it is not quiet. The script already knows the correct idiom - notify.sh:257 wraps the same class of failure as `if { : >/dev/tty; } 2>/dev/null; then` with the comment "the braces keep the no-tty redirection error off stderr" - so this is a self-inconsistency, not an unknown. The selftest cannot catch it: its only permissions fixture chmods `.gogo/work` (notify.sh:368), never `.gogo` itself, so the unwritable-.gogo path has zero coverage.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, two lines plus a fixture. Use the brace form the file already uses at :257: `{ printf '%s\n' "$current" > "$root/.gogo/.notify-gates"; } 2>/dev/null || true` and `{ : > "$root/.gogo/.notify-gates"; } 2>/dev/null || true`. Then add a selftest root whose `.gogo` is chmod 555 (guarded by the same `[ "$(id -u)" != "0" ]` check the `unread` fixture uses, and chmod'd back before the find -delete cleanup) that runs the whole script without DRYRUN and asserts stderr contains NO `Permission denied` while the exit code is still 0 - the case that would have caught this.
issues.fix_summary: Both writes use the brace idiom ({ printf > f; } 2>/dev/null || true), mkdir -p quiet-guarded. New readonly-gogo selftest case (chmod 555 .gogo, non-root): asserts no Permission denied on stderr and exit 0. --- VERIFIED (round 3): both writes use the brace idiom the file already used for the tty write (notify.sh:176 and :178) and the new mkdir is quiet-guarded (:174). Proven where it was reported: with .gogo/resources/notify pre-existing and mode 555, HEAD writes NOTHING to stderr and exits 0, while an unbraced mutant of the same code prints ".../notify/gates: Permission denied". The new readonly-gogo case (notify.sh:526-545) is id -u guarded and restores mode 755 at :544, before the find -delete cleanup at :550, so it cannot strand the temp tree - and because gogo_selftest is invoked from an `if` condition, errexit is suppressed for its whole body, so no intermediate failure can jump past that chmod. One caveat, filed separately as REV-016 rather than reopening this: that case exercises the mkdir guard only, never the brace guard it was added to protect.

issues.title: The new .gogo/.notify-gates state file is neither gitignored nor listed in the .gogo/ tree enumeration - every gogo-wired repo grows an untracked file gogo is forbidden to ignore for the user
issues.description: D4 introduced the first machine-local mutable file at the `.gogo/` ROOT. VERIFIED: `git check-ignore -v .gogo/.notify-gates` returns rc=1 (not ignored) in this repo, and `.gogo/` is a tracked directory here (1014 tracked files under it), so the file surfaces as untracked in `git status` and is one `git add -A` away from being committed - a per-machine, per-checkout latch landing in shared history, where it would then suppress other developers' first gate ping. The blast radius is not just gogo's own repo: the hook writes into `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.gogo/` of EVERY project gogo is wired into, and non-functional-requirements.md:26 forbids the remedy of just fixing it there ("Don't auto-edit `.gitignore`; print guidance instead" - restated at skills/gogo-build/SKILL.md:245 and docs/discovery.md:112). Second, the file is missing from the `.gogo/` enumeration in docs/architecture.md's "Project side (created in your repo)" tree (~line 168, which lists knowledge/ · skills/ · resources/ · changelog/ · work/), which coding-rules.md "Keep enumerations in sync" covers; that specific block is NOT among the phase-5 reconcile targets plan.md:319-321 lists (it names architecture.md:137, the plugin-side hooks line).
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Preferred: move the latch under the already-ignored, already-sanctioned regenerable root - `.gogo/resources/notify/gates` (`.gitignore` line `.gogo/resources/` covers it verbatim, docs/cli-contract.md:185 already calls that root the place for CLI/runtime scratch, and it needs no user .gitignore edit at all). `gogo_notify_remember` then does `mkdir -p "$root/.gogo/resources/notify" 2>/dev/null || true` before the write and keeps its existing best-effort guards; `gogo_notify_new_gates` follows the path. Alternative if the root path must stay: add `.gogo/.notify-gates` to this repo's `.gitignore` AND have `/gogo:build` print it as guidance for wired projects (never auto-edit). Either way, add the file to docs/architecture.md's project-side `.gogo/` tree and update README.md/docs/flow.md's `.gogo/.notify-gates` mentions if the path moves.
issues.fix_summary: Seen-file moved to .gogo/resources/notify/gates - verified covered by .gitignore:17 (.gogo/resources/). No user .gitignore edit needed; docs/architecture.md project tree already lists resources/. All doc/chart/plan references updated. --- VERIFIED (round 3): the preferred remedy, taken verbatim. `git check-ignore -v .gogo/resources/notify/gates` -> `.gitignore:17:.gogo/resources/`; a live hook probe in this repo created the file and `git status --porcelain .gogo/resources` stayed empty, so nothing new is untracked and no user .gitignore edit is needed. The destination is the project's established runtime/scratch root (docs/cli-contract.md:185 - the CLI's locks, session registry and logs already live under it), so the latch adds no new class of artifact to a wired repo. Every product reference moved together (notify.sh:20,153,159,173,503 - README.md:676 - docs/flow.md:213 - plan.md:152 - charts/flow.mmd, charts/sequence.mmd, charts/manifest.json); the only surviving `.gogo/.notify-gates` strings are in decisions.md's historical D4 record, which carries an explicit round-3 "moved to" note. Residue judged not worth reopening: docs/architecture.md:167 enumerates resources/'s contents (viewer/, view/, kanban/) without notify/ - but that same line already omits resources/cli/, and plan.md's checklist item 7 routes architecture.md to the phase-5 knowledge reconcile.

issues.title: The gate scan runs twice per gate-class notification - 45% of the hook's latency is duplicated work that grows linearly with the feature count
issues.description: For `class=gate` at `level=gates` (the most common event - `agent_completed` fires once per subagent hand-off), `gogo_notify_decide` scans every state.md at notify.sh:207 and computes verdict/gates/msg, then `gogo_notify_main` throws all of it away and scans again at notify.sh:282 to run the latch. MEASURED in this repo (31 `.gogo/work/feature-*` dirs, 5 runs each, DRYRUN): a gate-class invocation costs **816 ms** while a silent-class invocation, which does no scan at all, costs **74 ms** - so ~742 ms is scan and ~371 ms of that is a verbatim repeat. Cost is one awk + one grep subprocess per feature folder per pass, i.e. it scales linearly: an older tree with 100 work items would spend ~2.5 s deciding whether to buzz. Not a correctness defect and not on the CLI read path the performance bar governs, but it is needless re-fetch on the hook's hot path and the fix is small.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, pick one: (a) have `gogo_notify_decide` skip the gate scan when the caller will redo it - e.g. main sets an internal flag - which is the least invasive but adds a mode; (b) move the latch READ into `gogo_notify_decide` (reading `.gogo/.notify-gates` is still side-effect-free, so decide stays testable) and leave ONLY the one-line `gogo_notify_remember` write in main. (b) is the better shape: it removes the second scan, and it also makes the ~20 gate-class selftest `expect` cases assert the SHIPPED verdict instead of the pre-latch one (see REV-015), at the cost of giving the affected fixtures an explicit seen-file setup. Whichever is chosen, re-measure and record the before/after ms in the fix summary (the diagnosability bar: a limit must name its number).
issues.fix_summary: Option (b): latch READ moved into decide (still side-effect-free); main only remembers, from decide gatelist field - no second scan. Measured in this 31-feature repo: gate-class 816ms -> ~430ms (3 runs: 460/430/430), silent-class ~80ms unchanged. --- VERIFIED (round 3): option (b), as recommended. gogo_notify_main no longer calls gogo_notify_gates at all - it decodes decide's gatelist field and re-remembers it (notify.sh:288-299), so the state.md scan runs exactly once per invocation. Re-measured here (31 feature folders, DRYRUN, wall clock): gate-class 457 / 530 / 538 ms against the round-2 baseline of 816 ms; silent-class 139-156 ms, unchanged (it still does no scan). The halving matches one scan instead of two. decide stays side-effect-free - the latch READ only reads - which is what keeps --selftest able to drive it directly.

issues.title: charts/manifest.json's note and diagram titles predate the D4 latch, so the as-built manifest describes a pipeline its own .mmd files no longer draw
issues.description: `charts/flow.mmd` and `charts/sequence.mmd` were rewritten for the latch (flow.mmd:18-21 adds the `edge-latch (D4): NEW vs .gogo/.notify-gates?` decision node and the `remember pruned set` sink; sequence.mmd:26-28 adds `(newly opened)` and the remember note) - but `charts/manifest.json` was last written at 15:52 while both .mmd files are stamped 18:00, and its prose never caught up. The manifest `note` walks the pipeline as "the GOGO_NOTIFY_LEVEL switch, the gogo_notify_classify() type classifier ... and the gogo_notify_gates() scan" and stops there - no latch, no `.notify-gates`, no D4. The flow diagram's `title` likewise enumerates "level switch -> type classifier -> state.md gate scan -> send or stay silent" with the latch node missing, and the sequence `title` says the event "pings once when phase 5 writes awaiting-uat" without the latch that is now the diagram's new content. These `title` strings are not decoration: they are the typed charts-manifest contract and the captions `/gogo:view` renders and the phase-5 report bundle carries, so the drift is user-visible. code-review-standards.md #1 (every surface that describes the changed behaviour in sync).
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, docs only. Rewrite `charts/manifest.json`'s `note` to include the D4 edge-latch stage (gate set diffed against `.gogo/.notify-gates`, pruned set re-remembered, missing/unreadable file degrades to fire-on-open-gate) and extend both `title` strings to name it - e.g. flow: "... -> state.md gate scan -> D4 edge-latch vs .gogo/.notify-gates -> send or stay silent"; sequence: "... and the same event pings once when phase 5 writes awaiting-uat, after which the latch keeps the parked gate silent". Re-validate against templates/contracts/charts-manifest.schema.json.
issues.fix_summary: manifest.json note + both titles now name the D4 edge-latch stage and the .gogo/resources/notify/gates path; re-checked against charts-manifest.schema.json (fields, kinds, .mmd paths). --- VERIFIED (round 3): charts/manifest.json's note now walks the D4 stage explicitly (open-gate set diffed against .gogo/resources/notify/gates, pruned set re-remembered by main after every gate-class event, missing/unreadable seen-file degrades to fire-on-open-gate, never to silence), and both diagram titles name the latch and the path. Re-validated against templates/contracts/charts-manifest.schema.json: required slug/diagrams present, slug matches the pattern, both kinds are in the enum, both file values match \.mmd$ and exist on disk, no additional properties. The .mmd sources match the as-built shape (flow.mmd:18-21 latch decision + dotted remember sink; sequence.mmd:26-28 "(newly opened)" + the remember note).

issues.title: gogo_notify_decide is still documented as "the whole decision" although main now overrides its gate verdict - and gogo_notify_new_gates assigns a `root` local it never reads
issues.description: Two small truth/hygiene defects in the new latch code. (1) hooks/notify.sh:176 still reads "The whole decision, side-effect-free (the selftest calls this; main sends)". Since D4 that is false for the class the feature is about: for `class=gate` at `level=gates`, `gogo_notify_main` recomputes `verdict`, `gates` and `msg` (notify.sh:280-297), so decide's answer is discarded. The practical consequence is already visible in the suite - roughly twenty `expect` cases under the "FR4 - agent_completed is gate-conditional" heading assert a verdict that is NOT what the hook ships for that input once the gate is latched (e.g. `completed-uat` asserts notify; production is silent on the second event). Nothing is wrong today, but the comment invites the next maintainer to add a decide() consumer and get latch-free behaviour, and it is the same blind spot that let REV-010 through. (2) notify.sh:155 declares `local root="${1:-}"` in `gogo_notify_new_gates` and never uses it (the function reads `$1` again to build `seen`) - a dead assignment shellcheck would flag SC2034.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. (1) Retitle the comment to what it now is, e.g. "The type/level decision, side-effect-free. For class=gate the FINAL verdict is formed in gogo_notify_main, which applies the D4 latch - see the latch block there", and add a one-line note above the FR4 `expect` block saying those cases pin the pre-latch gate verdict while the latch cases pin the shipped one. If REV-013(b) is taken, this resolves itself - the latch read moves into decide and the comment becomes true again. (2) Drop the unused `root` local (or use it: `seen="$root/.gogo/.notify-gates"`), which also removes the duplicated `${1:-}` expansion.
issues.fix_summary: decide() comment rewritten: it IS the whole decision incl. the latch read (REV-013b made it true); the write is documented as main-owned. Dead root local removed by the refactor (new_gates now uses $root for seen). Decide-level gate cases now assert the SHIPPED verdict. --- VERIFIED (round 3): notify.sh:183-191 now describes what the function actually does - the whole decision INCLUDING the D4 latch READ, with the WRITE explicitly attributed to gogo_notify_main - and REV-013(b) made that true rather than merely rewording it. The dead local is gone: gogo_notify_new_gates:157-159 now uses $root to build $seen. The decide-level gate cases do assert the shipped first-event verdict: instrumenting the suite shows only quiet/, gate-uat/ and gate-latch/ ever gain a latch file, and all three writes happen after the last `expect` case runs. That ordering dependence is the one thing left behind - filed as REV-019, a nit.

issues.title: The REV-011 regression guard is vacuous for the write it protects: with .gogo at 555 the mkdir short-circuits first, so deleting the brace guards keeps the selftest 42/42 green
issues.description: code-review-standards.md #11 / #12 ("an assertion that looks like a check and isn't"; a test whose comment claims coverage its assertions do not provide). The readonly-gogo case added this round (hooks/notify.sh:524-545) chmods the whole `.gogo` to 555 and its comment states "555 keeps the scan readable; the remember write fails". The write does not fail - it never runs. gogo_notify_remember now starts with `mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0` (notify.sh:174) where $dir is .gogo/resources/notify, and under a 555 .gogo that mkdir fails, so the function returns before reaching either redirection. PROVEN BY MUTATION, both directions: (a) restoring the pre-fix unbraced form at :176/:178 (`printf ... > "$dir/gates" 2>/dev/null || true`) leaves `bash hooks/notify.sh --selftest` at 42/42, exit 0 - the exact defect REV-011 reported is undetectable again; (b) removing only the mkdir's `2>/dev/null` correctly fails the case (41/42), which is all this fixture actually pins. The uncovered path is reachable in the real world: with .gogo/resources/notify already present but unwritable (or a root-owned `gates` file from a sudo'd run, or a read-only mount), HEAD is silent while the unbraced mutant prints "<path>/gates: Permission denied" to stderr on EVERY gate-class event - verified live in a temp tree. Deliberately NOT rated major (unlike REV-010, whose unpinned wiring hid the feature's central bug): the shipped code is correct and the uncovered blast radius is stderr noise on an exotic permissions path. It is still a guard that cannot bite.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, a two-line fixture change. Make the fixture fail at the WRITE, not at the mkdir: in the readonly-gogo setup, pre-create the target dir and lock that instead - `mkdir -p "$tmp/rogogo/.gogo/resources/notify"` then `chmod 555 "$tmp/rogogo/.gogo/resources/notify"` (leave .gogo itself writable), keeping the existing `id -u` guard and restoring 755 before the find -delete cleanup. Optionally keep the current 555-.gogo variant as a second case so BOTH guards (mkdir and the two redirections) are pinned. Acceptance criterion: with the fixture changed, re-running mutation (a) above - the unbraced `printf ... > "$dir/gates" 2>/dev/null` - must drop the suite below 42 and exit 1.
issues.fix_summary: New readonly-notify-dir case: notify/ dir pre-created then chmod 555, so mkdir -p succeeds and only the braced write fails. Un-brace mutation (python-patched copy) -> 42/43, exit 1 with the Permission denied leak named. Original rogogo case kept (it pins the mkdir quietness).

issues.title: plan.md FR6 still asserts "Nothing is written to disk" although the shipped hook writes the D4 latch file on every gate-class event - and now on dry runs too
issues.description: plan.md:170, inside FR6 ("The hook is observable"), reads: "GOGO_NOTIFY_DEBUG=1 prints one stderr line per invocation ... Nothing is written to disk." As built, hooks/notify.sh:296-299 writes .gogo/resources/notify/gates on EVERY class=gate invocation at level=gates - the most common event - and, as of this round's REV-010 fix, unconditionally, including under GOGO_NOTIFY_DRYRUN=1. plan.md is the phase contract (the artifact review, test and the phase-5 report all reason against), and the same file already demonstrates the convention for exactly this drift: FR4 carries an inline "*(As-built refinement, D4/REV-001: ...)*" note (plan.md:149-154) recording the latch, and decisions.md's D4 resolution explicitly accepts "one small mutable state file under .gogo/". So the write is sanctioned - only FR6's statelessness claim was left stale, which is code-review-standards.md #1 (no place still describes the old behaviour). Not a scope violation and not a code defect: the write is confined to .gogo/, gitignored, and user-approved. Two adjacent statements were checked and are still TRUE, so this is the only stale one: "Out of scope: a notification history / log file under .gogo/" (plan.md:354) - the latch is a state file, not a log - and the Approach sketch at plan.md:234-246, which is explicitly the pre-implementation recommendation rather than an as-built claim.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, one sentence, docs only. Amend plan.md:170 to match FR4's as-built convention, e.g. replace "Nothing is written to disk." with "*(As-built, D4: the one thing written to disk is the edge-latch's last-notified gate set at `.gogo/resources/notify/gates` - rewritten on every gate-class invocation, including under GOGO_NOTIFY_DRYRUN, which suppresses SENDING only. No log, no history; see FR4 and decisions.md D4.)*". Do not weaken the surrounding observability claim - the stderr trace is still the only DEBUG output.
issues.fix_summary: plan.md FR6 gained an as-built scope note: the DEBUG trace is stderr-only; the one disk artifact is D4s latch seen-file, written on gate-class events incl. dry runs.

issues.title: The new decide->main record joins the gatelist on "|", so a work-folder name containing "|" desyncs the latch and re-notifies that gate forever
issues.description: The 5-field record protocol added this round transports the gate set as one field joined with "|" (notify.sh:234 `joined="$(printf '%s' "$gatelist" | tr '\n' '|')"`) and main splits it back with `tr '|' '\n'` (notify.sh:298). The delimiter is not escaped and can occur in the payload: the payload lines are `<feature-folder> · <status>` and a directory name may contain "|" on any POSIX filesystem. VERIFIED in a temp tree with `.gogo/work/feature-a|b/` at awaiting-uat: the seen file is written as TWO lines ("feature-a" / "b · awaiting-uat"), neither of which can ever match the single scan line, so `grep -Fxv -f` reports the gate as new on every event - three consecutive agent_completed runs give notify, notify, notify, i.e. REV-001's per-hand-off spam returns permanently for that item. Rated a nit, not higher, on two counts: reachability is low (folder names come from gogo-plan's "derive a kebab-case slug" step, though that is LLM prose with no mechanical enforcement - the same class of assumption coding-rules.md warns about elsewhere), and the failure degrades to NOISY, which is the direction non-functional-requirements.md explicitly prefers ("degrade to MISSING over WRONG"; the latch's own comment promises "never to silence"). The "-" empty-list placeholder was checked separately and is sound: every real line contains " · ", so a legitimate gatelist can never be the literal "-", and the placeholder is genuinely required because tab is IFS whitespace (an empty middle field would collapse and shift `msg` left - reproduced).
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, two characters. Join and split on a byte that cannot appear in a path component - e.g. ASCII unit separator: `tr '\n' '\037'` at notify.sh:234 and `tr '\037' '\n'` at notify.sh:298 (bash/BSD/GNU tr all accept the octal escape; the selftest already runs under bash 3.2 and 5.3, so re-run both). Keep the "-" placeholder and its comment as they are. Optionally add one selftest case with a folder name containing the delimiter, asserting run1 notify + run2 silent, so the round trip is pinned rather than assumed.
issues.fix_summary: Outside the contract: a feature slug is ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ and a status token shares that alphabet, so no legitimate gate line can contain "|". A comment above the join documents the invariant; hand-made folder names outside the slug grammar are out of scope for the hook (the CLI readers reject them too).

issues.title: The e2e selftest cases write latch state into two fixture roots shared with a dozen decide-level cases, so the suite is now order-dependent
issues.description: Since the latch READ moved into gogo_notify_decide (REV-013b), a fixture root that has been through a whole-script run behaves differently for every later `expect` on it. Instrumenting the suite before its cleanup shows exactly three roots gain .gogo/resources/notify/gates: gate-latch/ (its own, by design) but also quiet/ and gate-uat/ - and those two are shared: $tmp/gate-uat backs a dozen cases (needs-gate, perm-gate, idle-gate, the six silent-* types, completed-uat, unknown-gate, level-off) and $tmp/quiet backs ten more. Today the suite is CORRECT only because the two e2e cases at notify.sh:468 and :478 run after every `expect`, and because the gate-uat expectations that remain silent (silent-*, level-off) short-circuit before the gate scan anyway - so no case currently passes for the wrong reason (checked case by case). But this is the fixture-reuse shape code-review-standards.md #11(c) names ("a fixture reused its data home so the other arm block re-tested the first arm"): move or add a gate-class `expect` on gate-uat below line 468 and it silently becomes a latch test - a `notify` expectation fails confusingly, a `silent` expectation passes for the latch reason rather than the intended one.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, two lines. Give the two e2e cases their own roots the way the latch block already does - `mk_state "$tmp/e2e-gate" feature-e '- **status:** awaiting-uat'` and `mk_state "$tmp/e2e-quiet" feature-q '- **status:** implementing'` - and point notify.sh:468/:478 at them, so no root is ever both a decide-level fixture and a whole-script fixture. Add one line to the block comment stating the invariant ("a root that a whole-script run touches must not back any expect case") so the next case lands correctly.
issues.fix_summary: The two whole-script e2e cases got DEDICATED roots (e2e-gate, e2e-quiet) so the latch write can never leak into roots the expect-level cases read, regardless of case ordering.
